W1 (mechanism), after E015.

The setup
- The tip is E015: the E010 recipe (Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs, about 238 steps, widths 128/384/512) with the train step under max-autotune CUDA graphs.
- It scores 6.578 s and 0.75743.
- Graph capture saved only 0.06 s (−0.9%). The +0.27 pp accuracy change is a kernel-path reshuffle, not a real gain: the math is identical, so it is noise. The tip's "true" mean is probably about 0.756, and part of its 0.44 pp margin is luck.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time (E003/E004).
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time, about −0.6 pp; a 20 px stage is a cliff, −1 pp, because the group-3 maps shrink to 2×2 (E007/E011).
- Cutting 0.5 epoch: −0.18 pp, −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576→512: −0.25 pp, −4.8% time (E010).
- CUDA graphs: −0.9% time (E015).
- Scalar retunes are flat within ±0.1 pp: LR floor (E009), label smoothing (E013), Muon lr ×1.5 (E014).
- So the gains came from structural changes. A scalar retune worth ≥0.3 pp has a prior of about 10%.

Weight decay
- Muon has no weight-decay term and renormalizes the filters to a fixed norm.
- So weight decay touches only the BatchNorm biases, the whitening bias and the head. Halving it is expected to change accuracy by about 0, ±0.15 pp, plus a reshuffle.

Time model
- Training is GPU-bound: about 26 ms per step at batch 2000.
- E015 confirms that launch overhead is about 1%.
- The remaining host-side cost is a fixed ~0.3-0.4 s:
  - the host-to-GPU copy;
  - the eigendecomposition;
  - the pad;
  - the augment, which does 25 boolean-mask copies per epoch with host syncs;
  - interpolate and the permutation gathers for each resolution.
- Removing the remaining syncs might save 0.05-0.15 s (1-2%), not ≥3%.
- Real time levers are FLOPs: epochs, width, resolution fraction (e.g. 24 px for 50% of steps instead of 40%), and possibly a narrower group 2.
- Time repeats within 1%.

Accuracy model
- Endpoint averaging dominates. The alpha ramp 0.95^5·(k/T)^3 means the EMA tracks the live weights early and averages over about 20 steps at the end.
- The Lookahead reset also damps fast-weight noise at the LR floor.
- A plain EMA without write-back probably keeps most of the gain but loses about 0.1-0.3 pp. The fast weights wander more, and the averaged BN buffers mismatch the averaged weights slightly more.
- Exchange rates for buying time with accuracy:
  - epochs: about 0.37 pp per 10% time;
  - width: about 0.5 pp per 10%;
  - moderate resizing: about 0.27 pp per 10%.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical for an unchanged recipe (E012).
- Any change to the kernel or RNG path reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp (E015: +0.27 pp with identical math). Seed std is about 0.25 pp.
- Treat 0.7574 as a lucky draw from about 0.756 ± 0.15.

Unsure
- The held-out seed offset, still not reported. It decides whether the 0.44 pp margin can be spent on about 0.5 epoch (−5% time) or a larger 24 px fraction.
- Whether the compiled augment changes the RNG stream, which would reshuffle accuracy.
- Whether any remaining structural lever (EMA schedule, BN momentum, whitening variant) adds ≥0.3 pp that could be spent on epochs.

forecasts.reason: Muon filters carry no weight decay and are norm-fixed, so halving it touches only the biases and head; expect about 0 plus a ±0.2 pp reshuffle, likely regressing from the lucky 0.7574.

CUDA graphs already cut launch cost to about 1%; the remaining syncs in augment and the LR loop are worth about 0.05-0.15 s, short of 3%, and compiling the augment likely changes the RNG path, so accuracy won't be bit-identical.
Without the Lookahead reset, the fast weights stay noisier at the LR floor and the end average is worse; expect a loss of about 0.1-0.3 pp, near the 0.3 pp threshold and within noise.

cruxes: What is the held-out seed mean (seeds 3-12) for the E015 tip? Is 0.7574 a lucky reshuffle (true mean about 0.756), or real margin that can pay for cutting about 0.5 epoch (−5% time)?

How much of the 6.58 s is fixed host-side cost (the copy, the eigendecomposition, augment syncs, permutation gathers) versus per-step GPU compute? Per-epoch CUDA-event timing would show whether systems trims can still give more than 2%.
Does any structural accuracy lever not yet tried (EMA/Lookahead schedule, BN momentum, a larger fraction of steps at 24 px with a later EMA ramp) give at least 0.3 pp that can be spent on FLOPs?
